reader.requirement: At --std 85 the order in which a sequential file's records are read back must be the order in which the WRITE statements that created it executed, unchanged by a REWRITE, extended only by records added at the end (OPEN EXTEND, including on a created optional file), and established afresh when OPEN OUTPUT creates the file again; this holds for fixed, variable-length (RECORD VARYING / ODO) and multi-description records.

edition-consulted.switches: SharingFacilityInEffect: from 2002 every WRITE is flushed to the medium; at 85 a connector buffers while it is the only connector on the physical file and flushes per record once a sibling is open
at 85 (no sharing facility) each connector already open on the file releases its buffered records before an incoming OPEN's body runs

reader.edition-search: grep SharingFacilityInEffect/Edition/DialectBehavior over SequentialConnector.cs, FileConnector.cs and FileRegistry.cs on the WRITE and OPEN EXTEND paths
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the order of records; yes for when a WRITE reaches the medium (85 buffers a lone connector's records), which the 85 arm compensates for at a sibling's OPEN
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_02 covers fixed-length records, REWRITE in place and EXTEND on an existing and an empty file; variable-length records, multi-description FDs, an optional file created by EXTEND, re-creation by OUTPUT and two connectors appending to one file (the 85 buffering arm) are not exercised

probes.printed: LAST WRITE 00 / RW 00 / V 5 E 06 / V 1 Z 02 / V 8 H 09 / V 3 C 04 / W LONGONE / W S01GONE / W LONGTWO / W S02GTWO / X OPEN 05 / X N01
probes.expected: write order kept for variable-length records with their lengths, REWRITE in place, EXTEND at the end; FD with two record lengths keeps order; optional file created by EXTEND (05); OUTPUT re-creates the file with a new relationship

probes.printed: FB OPEN 00 / A R01 / A R02 / A R03 / A R04 / A R05
probes.expected: two connectors appending to one physical file at 85 (the buffering arm): records read back in the order of the WRITE executions

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR12  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12

reader.notes: The one 85-specific arm on this path is the release policy (buffer while alone, release before a sibling's OPEN, flush per record while a sibling is open); the probe with two appending connectors shows the order of execution survives it. A first probe run without setting the DEPENDING ON item failed its WRITEs (VL=0 below the minimum), a probe error and not a finding.

refuter.evidence: q4a.cob (runs/q4a-001): RECORD VARYING 2..6 DEPENDING ON VL. OUTPUT A1,B22, a WRITE below the minimum (44, adds nothing), C333; CLOSE WITH NO REWIND (07); EXTEND D4444; I-O REWRITE of record 2 to b22; EXTEND E55555. Forward read: A1 2, b22 3, C333 4, D4444 5, E55555 6, then 10. The 1985-only OPEN INPUT ... REVERSED (obsolete, level 2) reads the same relationship backwards: E55555, D4444, C333, b22, A1, then 10. The order is the WRITE order, unchanged by REWRITE and by the failed WRITE, extended only at the end. Citations: OK §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR12 (the text is in GR12).
